W-2 and 1099-NEC deadlines for tax year 2026 and how to correct a form already filed
Forms W-2 and W-3 for 2026 wages are due February 1, 2027 (January 31 is a Sunday), and employees generally get their W-2 copies by the same date. Form 1099-NEC for 2026 payments is due Monday, February 1, 2027, to the IRS and the recipient, because the January 31 due date moves to the next business day. A W-2 already filed with the Social Security Administration is corrected on Form W-2c, and a filed 1099-NEC with a corrected return.
Who receives each form, and what triggers a filing?
Copy A of Form W-2 goes to the Social Security Administration (SSA) with Form W-3, and each employee receives their own copies. Form 1099-NEC goes to the IRS, and the recipient gets a statement. The IRS instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 and for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC allow either paper or electronic filing, subject to the e-file rule below.


For 2026 payments, the reporting threshold is $2,000 for Form 1099-NEC payments for services performed by someone who is not an employee and for W-2 wages paid without withholding, and the IRS says the amount may be adjusted for inflation beginning in calendar year 2027. State and local reporting varies by state, so employers check with their state, city, or local tax department.
How do the e-file and extension rules work?
E-filing is required once an employer files 10 or more information returns in total, and the IRS counts W-2s and 1099s together. The instructions say a filer at that level must e-file them all. Corrected returns are not included in that count, and filing on paper when e-filing is required can draw a penalty.


For Form W-2, the SSA accepts only e-filed reports and the official red-ink paper forms or approved substitute versions, not a printout of Copy A, and it decommissioned its previous online W-2 filing application on September 19, 2026.


For Form 1099-NEC, the IRS offers IRIS, a free portal for up to 100 returns at a time that needs an IRIS Transmitter Control Code (TCC), plus an application-to-application (A2A) option for software. As of October 2026, the last day to file information returns through the older FIRE system is November 19, 2026, at 3 p.m. ET, and current FIRE users must move to IRIS to file tax year 2026 information returns.


For Forms W-2 and 1099-NEC, no automatic extension is available. An employer can request one 30-day extension on Form 8809, which must be submitted on paper, filed before the due date, and based on a criterion the form lists, such as a federally declared disaster, fire or casualty, or the death or serious illness of the responsible person. The W-2 instructions limit the extension to extraordinary circumstances or catastrophe. No additional 30-day extension is allowed, and an extension does not extend the due date for furnishing statements to employees or recipients.


Extra time to furnish copies is a separate request on Form 15397. For Form W-2 copies, requests are not automatically granted, and an approved extension is generally no more than 15 days from the due date, unless the need for up to 30 days in total is clearly shown. For Form 1099 copies, an approved request generally gets a maximum of 30 extra days. The Form 1099 request goes by fax and must be received by the due date, and the IRS says not to mail it.
What are the penalty tiers for late or incorrect returns?
As of October 2026, the W-2 instructions set the penalty for filings due after December 31, 2026, by how late the correct return arrives.


When the correct return is filed
Penalty per Form W-2
Within 30 days of the due date
$60
More than 30 days after the due date, through August 1
$130
After August 1, or when a required return or correction is never filed
$340
Intentional disregard
At least $690, with no maximum


A penalty for incorrect or late employee copies is additional and applied in the same manner. The IRS indexes the amounts for inflation, and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 states the same tiers for returns required to be filed in 2027, so they apply to Form 1099-NEC as well.


The W-2 instructions describe relief for reasonable cause, a de minimis rule for corrections, and a safe harbor for small dollar errors. The de minimis rule applies to returns filed by the required filing date that were missing information or contained incorrect information, and it covers the greater of 10 information returns or 0.5% of the total information returns required to be filed for the year, as long as corrections are filed by August 1. The safe harbor generally applies when no single amount in error differs from the correct amount by more than $100 and no single amount of tax withheld differs by more than $25. If the payee elects for the safe harbor not to apply, a corrected return may be needed to avoid penalties. For reasonable cause, a filer that receives Notice 972CG should respond within 45 days, before the IRS assesses the penalty.


Hypothetical example. An employer has 40 W-2s due February 1, 2027, no relief applies, and employee copies go out on time. Filed correctly by March 3, 2027, which is 30 days after the due date, the exposure is 40 × $60 = $2,400. Filed March 15, 2027, it is 40 × $130 = $5,200. Filed August 16, 2027, it is 40 × $340 = $13,600.
How do you correct a W-2 that is already filed?
If the employee has the W-2 but Copy A has not gone to the SSA, void the Copy A form, prepare a new W-2, send its Copy A to the SSA, and give the employee copies marked CORRECTED. Do not write CORRECTED on Copy A.


Once Copy A is with the SSA, use Form W-2c with Form W-3c, filed as soon as possible after the error is found. Form W-2c copies go to the SSA (Copy A), the state (Copy 1), the employee (Copies B, C and 2) and the employer (Copy D). A W-2c must be e-filed if the original W-2 had to be e-filed, and must be filed on paper if the original was permitted on paper and filed that way.


To correct only a name or SSN, complete boxes d through i and do not complete boxes 1 through 20. Box d shows the correct SSN. Otherwise Copy A shows only the changed items, and when either the previously reported amount or the correct amount is zero, the box shows -0- rather than being left blank.


If the SSA copy has only an incorrect employee address, do not file a Form W-2c with the SSA. If the employee’s copy showed the wrong address, the employer must still correct it, for example with a new W-2 marked REISSUED STATEMENT or a Form W-2c given to the employee, without sending Copy A to the SSA. If only state or local data changes, the W-2c goes to the state or local agency rather than the SSA, and copies go to the employees. A wrong tax year or wrong EIN takes two sets of Forms W-2c and W-3c. A W-2c can also require corrections to previously filed employment tax returns through the matching X form, such as Form 941-X. An employee who amends a return because of the correction files Form 1040-X with Copy B. For code TT (qualified overtime compensation), IRS fact sheet FS-2026-13 says an employer that finds an error in the code must file a W-2c and furnish it to the employee as soon as possible, and an employee who reasonably believes the employer omitted or understated the amount must request a W-2c from the employer to use that amount in the overtime deduction.


Using a payroll provider or another third party does not relieve an employer of its responsibility for W-2 reporting, and the W-2 instructions strongly suggest that the address on record with the IRS be the employer’s address, not the third party’s address.
How do you correct a 1099-NEC that is already filed?
The error decides how many returns the fix takes. Under the paper error charts in Publication 1099, a wrong amount, code or checkbox takes one new return with the CORRECTED box checked. A missing or wrong taxpayer identification number (TIN), a wrong name or a wrong form type takes two returns. The first reports -0- for all money amounts, and the second is prepared as though it is an original. Each return type being corrected needs its own Form 1096.


Paper corrections follow part H of Publication 1099 and use the official Copy A rather than a printed PDF. Electronic corrections follow Publication 5717 for the IRIS portal or Publication 5718 for A2A, and a correction must be e-filed when the original return had to be. A correction to state or local information only is not sent to the IRS. Do not check the VOID box on a paper correction, because a correction with VOID checked is not entered into IRS records.


A TIN correction is not mandatory when the filer meets the reasonable-cause criteria, though the IRS encourages corrections for incorrect or missing TINs, and for a CP2100 response Publication 1281 says to refile only when the dollar amount is also changing.
What happens when a name and TIN do not match IRS records?
A CP2100 or CP2100A notice, which the IRS sends twice a year, in October and the following April, flags payees whose name and TIN are missing or do not match IRS records. A missing or obviously wrong TIN calls for backup withholding immediately and up to three requests for the TIN. For a name and TIN mismatch, when the notice is the first one received for that account and the payer’s records match the name and TIN listed on it, the payer sends a first B notice with a Form W-9 within 15 business days of the notice date or the date the notice was received, whichever is later. If no signed Form W-9 returns, backup withholding must begin no later than 30 business days after the notice date or the date it was received, whichever is later, and stops within 30 calendar days after the required certification arrives. Do not send the signed Form W-9 to the IRS. For a second CP2100 or CP2100A notice on the same account within three calendar years, the payer sends a second B notice without a Form W-9, and the payee must supply validation, such as a copy of a Social Security card for an individual or an IRS Letter 147C for an EIN. A second notice received in the same calendar year as the first can be disregarded.


As of October 2026, when backup withholding applies the rate is 24%, and it can apply to payments for work done as an independent contractor, according to the IRS backup withholding page. A payee who has applied for a TIN but has not yet furnished it is still subject to backup withholding on nonemployee compensation, because the awaiting-TIN exemption does not cover it. The withheld amount goes in box 4 of Form 1099-NEC and is reported on Form 945, and a 1099-NEC is required for backup withholding regardless of the amount of the payment.


Hypothetical example. A contractor with no TIN is owed $5,000. Backup withholding is 24% × $5,000 = $1,200, so the payer pays $3,800. The 1099-NEC shows the full $5,000 as nonemployee compensation and $1,200 in box 4, and Form 945 reports the $1,200.


Names and TINs can be checked before filing, and the check differs by worker. The SSA’s Social Security Number Verification Service (SSNVS) can be used only for current or former employees. For contractors, the IRS TIN Matching program lets payers match TIN and name combinations with IRS records, and the IRS suggests requesting a Form W-9 from each U.S. recipient.
Frequently asked questions
When are W-2s and 1099-NECs due for tax year 2026?
For tax year 2026, Forms W-2 and 1099-NEC are both due February 1, 2027, because January 31, 2027 is a Sunday and the 1099-NEC date follows the next-business-day rule.
Can an employer get an extension for W-2s or 1099-NECs?
No automatic extension is available for Form W-2 or Form 1099-NEC. An employer can request one 30-day extension on a paper Form 8809 filed before the due date, for a circumstance the form lists. An approved extension does not cover employee or recipient copies, and more time to furnish them takes a separate Form 15397 request, which is not automatically granted.
What is the penalty for a late or incorrect W-2 or 1099-NEC?
For returns due in 2027, before any relief, the penalty is $60, $130 or $340 per return, depending on when the correct return is filed, and at least $690 per return for intentional disregard. A late or incorrect employee or recipient copy carries an additional penalty at the same amounts.
How do you correct a W-2 that is already filed?
To correct a W-2 already filed with the SSA, file Form W-2c with Form W-3c as soon as the error is found, give the employee the W-2c copies, and e-file the correction if the original W-2 had to be e-filed. An error in only the employee’s address is not filed with the SSA, but the employee’s copy must still be corrected, and a change to only state or local data goes to the state or local agency rather than the SSA.
How do you correct a 1099-NEC that is already filed?
On a paper correction, a wrong amount, code or checkbox takes one new return with the CORRECTED box checked, while a missing or wrong TIN, a wrong name or a wrong form type takes two returns. Electronic corrections follow Publication 5717 for the IRIS portal or Publication 5718 for A2A.
What should an employer do when a contractor’s name and TIN do not match IRS records?
When a first CP2100 or CP2100A notice lists a name and TIN that match the payer’s records, send the first B notice with a Form W-9 within 15 business days of the notice date or the date the notice was received, whichever is later. If no signed Form W-9 comes back, backup withholding must begin no later than 30 business days after that date.
